steps.what: Evaluate existing computerized healthcare systems against clinical and information needs
Recommend upgrades or improvements based on the system evaluation

tasks.design: The technologist evaluates the healthcare system {OTHER} and discusses recommendations with its owner using evidence in {DOCS}. Existing test tools can support the evaluation without replacing decisions about clinical fit.
tasks.previous_blocker: A system can meet a technical specification yet fail the clinical workflow.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing diagnostics provide evidence but no common automatic evaluation covers local needs.
tasks.still_hard: Weighing clinical workflow, reliability, access and migration consequences.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist reconciles user needs with technical constraints.
tasks.altitude: Evaluation responsibility and recommendation authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Validate record-workflow requirements for an upgrade
reach.learn: Clinical record use and migration acceptance criteria

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: healthcare-system evaluation and improvement recommendations require local workflow judgement; no clerical test baseline is specified.

assumptions: Boundary is evaluation and recommendation, excluding implementation and separate formal acceptance testing.

OTHER means healthcare information system. Users and system owners supply needs and specifications under the existing review process; the technologist observes behaviour and produces findings in s1 before recommending changes in s2. No free suitability score is assumed.
Check native diagnostics first; existing test runtime earns no human saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new evaluation automation is introduced.
unknowns: System type and actual evaluation activities
research_questions: Which evaluation steps are repeated evidence gathering rather than judgement about clinical fit?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70+30=100; net 0%. Substantive evaluation and recommendation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Promote privacy and security awareness activities to staff
Facilitate lunches, seminars or tours about healthcare information privacy and security

tasks.design: The technologist promotes activities through {EMAIL} and facilitates discussion using current guidance from {DOCS}. Existing bulk-send runtime does not remove engagement or live facilitation work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Awareness depends on staff understanding and participation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing communication tools support outreach without establishing a new saving.
tasks.still_hard: Making guidance relevant to actual staff situations.
tasks.human_edge: The facilitator hears misconceptions and responds in context.
tasks.altitude: Awareness responsibility and contact time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Explain privacy risks in everyday record handling
reach.learn: Practical examples and staff learning needs

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: promotion and live facilitation require staff engagement; a bulk-email function alone does not establish saved labour.

assumptions: Boundary is promoting and facilitating activities, excluding separate course authoring and event administration.

The responsible privacy owner supplies current guidance; the technologist selects messages during s1. Participants supply questions during s2 after the activity begins; no structured comprehension flag is assumed.
Use native communications functions first; existing runtime earns no saving. Zero new upkeep because no new application or assessment is added.
research_questions: Which promotion activities are repeated clerical work rather than staff engagement?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+55=100; net 0%. Promotion and facilitation retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Identify patient records and verify the scope and classification version
Compile and abstract patient data and propose classification codes

loop.purpose: Propose coding and abstraction from selected clinical text
loop.input: Verified encounter records and applicable classification version
loop.output: Proposed fields and codes with supporting record passages and explicit uncertainty
loop.check: Registrar checks clinical meaning, principal versus secondary conditions, negation, timing and code specificity against the original record and classification guidance
loop.stop: One proposal and one correction pass; ambiguous or unsupported cases return to manual abstraction and clinician clarification
loop.why_not_simpler: Native thesaurus mappings handle already structured terms; free-text interpretation needs a bounded proposal step

steps.what: Check and assign the final patient classification codes

tasks.design: Use native thesaurus mappings in the clinical coding system {OTHER} first, then a bounded proposal for eligible free text. The registrar checks source meaning and assigns the exact final codes; the design does not automatically accept codes based on a confidence threshold.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant clinical facts are dispersed through narrative records.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked code proposals can support abstraction without replacing registrar judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous diagnoses, negation, chronology and classification-specific rules.
tasks.human_edge: The registrar identifies unsupported inference and obtains clinical clarification.
tasks.altitude: Less first-pass abstraction with coding accountability retained.

reach.learn: Clinical documentation queries and classification rules

evidence.claim: Dutch Hospital Data proposes ICD-10 main diagnoses from specialists' records for day admissions; this supports a bounded proposal capability, not all coding domains.
The provider reports use in 32 hospitals and 85-90% accuracy for its day-admission model; these figures do not establish local registrar time savings.
Model knowledge: the proposed abstraction time and review allowance are unmeasured scenarios requiring local validation.

assumptions: Boundary is registrar abstraction and coding, excluding original clinical documentation and downstream statistical reporting.

Clinicians produce the original record in existing care. In s1 the registrar verifies and captures patient and encounter IDs, record versions, coding scope, classification edition, authorised source passages and relevant dates; the full 30% remains. Missing or conflicting documentation goes to manual clarification, not inferred diagnosis.

OTHER means clinical record and coding system. Test native term-to-code mappings before model use. The proposed loop is limited to locally validated document and classification types; unsupported domains remain manual.

Six extra focal hours count model-change checks, sampled coding audits and failed proposals. Four other-role hours count coding-system administrator mapping and access maintenance. Existing coding runtime earns no new labour saving.
unknowns: Coding scope and local validation performance
Available source access and existing native mappings
research_questions: Does total abstraction time fall after checking every proposed code and handling ambiguous records?
Which negations and principal-diagnosis errors survive review?

already_counted.description: Scope verification and structured source capture

incremental.description: Model-change checks, coding audits and failed proposals
Coding administrator mapping and access maintenance

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient encounter, record versions, abstraction fields, code set and classification edition checked in s3; changed facts or codes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+45*0.65+25=84.25; gross 15.75%, net 9.75% after 6 focal upkeep. Range covers failed proposals with no gain through eligible clear records with 11 points of abstraction removed minus 6 upkeep. Source capture and final assignment remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Manage the department and supervise clerical workers' medical records activities

tasks.design: The technologist directs department work and responds to staff issues using existing records in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HCM}. No automatic worker evaluation or allocation based on performance is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervision involves changing workloads, individual needs and unresolved cases.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing work records support discussion without replacing management.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing service priorities with staff capacity and complex records issues.
tasks.human_edge: The manager listens, negotiates priorities and takes responsibility.

reach.task: Coordinate escalation of difficult records cases

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: department leadership and staff supervision remain human; a removable clerical baseline is not specified.

assumptions: Boundary is management and supervision, excluding clerical workers' processing and registrar coding in task 22900.
Staff provide work progress and concerns during s1; the manager assesses capacity and produces direction there. No free structured worker score is assumed.
Use native work records first; existing runtime earns no saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new management tool is added.
research_questions: Which managerial activities require direct staff discussion?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Leadership time remains and clerical workers' labour is excluded.
